questions.prompt: Do you know your neighbours well?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I know my neighbour. He is old. He is nice.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I know my neighbours. They are friendly. We say hello and sometimes we talk about the weather. But I don't know them very well.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I know some of my neighbours. I say hello when I see them. I think they are quite nice. For example, the lady next door sometimes brings me cake. However, I don't really know them very well, just a little.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, not as well as I probably should. We're on friendly terms — we always say hello and have a quick chat if we bump into each other — but I couldn't tell you much about their lives. The thing is, everyone's so busy these days that people tend to keep themselves to themselves, which is a bit of a shame.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men qo'shnimni bilaman. U keksa. U yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men qo'shnilarimni bilaman. Ular do'stona. Biz salomlashamiz va ba'zan ob-havo haqida gaplashamiz. Lekin men ularni juda yaxshi bilmayman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, men qo'shnilarimning bir qanchasini bilaman. Ularni ko'rsam, salom beraman. Menimcha, ular juda yaxshi odamlar.
Masalan, qo'shni ayol ba'zan menga tort olib keladi.
Lekin, men ularni unchalik yaxshi bilmayman, faqat ozgina.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men qo'shnilarimni *yaxshi* bilaman deb ayta olmayman, lekin ularni taniyman va biz xushmuomalalik qilamiz. Ularning ba'zilari haqida ozgina bilaman, masalan, ko'chaning narigi tomonida yashovchi oila – ularning ikki nafar yosh bolasi bor. O'ylaymanki, do'stona bo'lish muhim, hatto chuqur suhbatlarga vaqtim bo'lmasa ham. Bu mahallada yanada ijobiy muhit yaratadi va atrofingizda kim yashashini bilish yaxshi, har ehtimolga qarshi.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you know your neighbours well?
idioms: good fences make good neighbours - "yaxshi devor yaxshi qo'shni qiladi"
the grass is always greener on the other side - "boshqaning tomorqasi yashilroq ko'rinadi"
sentenceStarters: "To be honest, I don't know…" - "Rostini aytsam, men …ni yaxshi bilmayman"
"I think this is quite common in…" - "Menimcha, bu …da juda keng tarqalgan"

questions.sampleAnswer:
To be honest, I don't know my neighbours particularly well. We exchange greetings when we see each other in the hallway, but we've never really had a proper conversation.
I think this is quite common in big cities where people tend to keep to themselves. That said, I'd love to get to know them better because having good neighbours can make a real difference to your quality of life.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, qo'shnilarimni unchalik yaxshi bilmayman. Yo'lakda ko'rishganimizda salomlashamiz, lekin hech qachon chinakam suhbatlashmaganmiz.

O'ylashimcha, bu katta shaharlarda odamlar o'ziga qarab yurishi odatiy hol. Shunga qaramay, men ularni yaxshiroq bilishni xohlardim, chunki yaxshi qo'shnilar hayot sifatiga katta ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: What kind of things usually make you laugh?
questions.sampleA1:
I like funny videos. They are funny.

My friend is funny too.
questions.sampleA2:
I like funny things. I like when my friends tell jokes, and I laugh.

Sometimes I watch funny movies on TV and I laugh because they are silly.
questions.sampleB1:
Well, I usually laugh when I watch comedies on TV. I think they are very funny.

Also, I laugh when I'm with my friends because we always tell jokes and funny stories. For example, yesterday my friend told a story about...
questions.sampleB2: Loads of things, actually — I'd say I'm easy to please. Silly memes and funny videos online always crack me up, especially the ones with animals doing daft things. But honestly, nothing beats being with my close friends. We've got so many inside jokes that one look is enough to set us off. I suppose I just find humour everywhere.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Menga kulgili videolar yoqadi. Ular kulgili.

Do'stim ham kulgili.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menga kulgili narsalar yoqadi. Do'stlarim hazil aytganda yoqadi va men kulaman.

Ba'zan televizorda kulgili filmlar ko'raman va ular ahmoqona bo'lgani uchun kulaman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, men odatda televizorda komediyalarni ko'rsam kulaman. Menimcha, ular juda kulgili.

Shuningdek, do'stlarim bilan bo'lganimda ham kulaman, chunki biz doim hazillar va kulgili hikoyalar aytamiz. Masalan, kecha do'stim bir hikoya aytib berdi...
questions.uzSampleB2:
Menimcha, ko'p narsalar meni kuldira oladi, aslida. Men juda oson kuladigan odamman.

Aniqrog'i, men kundalik hayotning bema'niliklarini ko'rsatib beradigan kuzatuv komediyasi va stand-up chiqishlaridan zavqlanaman. Shuningdek, men oilam va do'stlarim bilan birga bo'lganimda ko'p kulaman; ularning ahmoqona hazillari va hikoyalari meni doim kuldiradi.

O'ylaymanki, hayotda, hatto qiyin vaziyatlarda ham hazil topish muhim.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - What kind of things usually make you laugh?
idioms: laughter is the best medicine - "kulgi — eng yaxshi davo"
sentenceStarters: "I'd say I have a fairly good…" - "Menimcha, menda yaxshi…bor"
"I also find that spending time with…" - "Shuningdek, …bilan vaqt o'tkazish…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd say I have a fairly good sense of humour and a lot of things can make me laugh. I particularly enjoy witty comedies and funny videos on social media — they always brighten my day.
I also find that spending time with close friends tends to lead to a lot of laughter, especially when we share inside jokes or recall embarrassing memories together. I think laughter is truly the best medicine.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, hazil-mutoyibaga yaxshi tushunaman va ko'p narsalar meni kuldira oladi. Ayniqsa, o'tkir hazillarga boy komediyalarni va ijtimoiy tarmoqlardagi kulgili videolarni yaxshi ko'raman — ular doim kayfiyatimni ko'taradi.

Yana shuni ham aytishim mumkinki, yaqin do'stlarim bilan vaqt o'tkazish ko'pincha ko'p kulgiga olib keladi, ayniqsa, o'zimizga xos hazillarimizni baham ko'rsak yoki birgalikda uyatli xotiralarni eslasak. O'ylashimcha, kulgu haqiqatan ham eng yaxshi dori.

questions.prompt: Do you often wear hats or caps?
questions.sampleA2: No, I don't wear hats. But my brother wears a hat because he likes it. He has a blue hat.
questions.sampleB1: Not really. I don't often wear hats or caps. Sometimes I wear a hat when it's very sunny, especially in the summer. I think hats are useful for that. However, I don't usually wear them for fashion.
questions.sampleB2: Not really, to be honest — I'm not much of a hat person. I'll throw on a cap in summer to keep the sun out of my eyes, and a woolly hat is a must when it gets freezing in winter. But other than that, I hardly ever wear them. I just find them a bit of a faff, I suppose.
questions.uzSampleA2: Yo'q, men shapka kiymayman. Lekin akam shapka kiyadi, chunki unga yoqadi. Uning ko'k shapkasi bor.
questions.uzSampleB1: Unchalik emas. Men ko'pincha shlyapa yoki kepka kiymayman. Ba'zan, juda quyoshli bo'lganda, ayniqsa yozda, shlyapa kiyaman. O'ylashimcha, shlyapalar shu uchun foydali. Biroq, men odatda ularni moda uchun kiymayman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men o'zimni doimiy shapka kiyadigan odam deb ayta olmayman. Ammo, shunday holatlar bo'ladiki, ularsiz ilojim yo'q deb bilaman. Misol uchun, sovuq oylarda jun shapka isinish uchun zarur. Xuddi shunday, yozda quyosh nuridan himoyalanish uchun beysbolka kiyishim mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ularni garderobimning asosiy qismi deb hisoblamayman.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you often wear hats or caps?
sentenceStarters: "Not particularly often, to be honest…" - "Rostini aytsam, unchalik tez-tez emas…"
"I sometimes wear a cap in…" - "Men ba'zan …da kepka kiyaman…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Not particularly often, to be honest. I sometimes wear a cap in the summer to shield myself from the sun, or a warm hat in winter when temperatures drop.
I wouldn't say I'm a big hat person in terms of fashion, but I do appreciate their practical benefits. Some people can really pull off a stylish hat, but I tend to keep it simple.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, unchalik ham emas. Ba'zan yozda quyoshdan saqlanish uchun kepka kiyaman, yoki qishda harorat pasayganda issiq shapka kiyaman.

Men moda nuqtai nazaridan katta shapka muxlisi emasman, lekin ularning amaliy foydalarini qadrlayman. Ba'zi odamlar haqiqatan ham zamonaviy shapkani juda yaxshi yarashira olishadi, lekin men sodda bo'lishga harakat qilaman.

questions.sampleB2: In the first picture, two young men are repairing a bright green bicycle in what looks like their living room. vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: reinvent the wheel - "g'ildirakni qayta ixtiro qilmoq (keraksiz takrorlash)"
phrases: self-service city station - "o'z-o'ziga xizmat ko'rsatuvchi shahar stansiyasi"
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I can see…" - "Birinchi rasmda men ko'ryapman…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In the first picture, I can see people repairing a bicycle in a small workshop. They appear to be carefully fixing the mechanical parts, which suggests they take good care of their own bike.
In the second picture, people are renting bicycles from a self-service city station — it looks like a modern bike-sharing system. The contrast between the two images highlights the difference between personal ownership and the growing trend of shared mobility in cities.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:

Ikkala rasm o'rtasidagi farq shaxsiy egalik va shaharlarda ommalashib borayotgan umumiy mobillik tendentsiyasi o'rtasidagi farqni ta'kidlaydi.

Because you can save money, for example, you don't need to go to the shop.

questions.sampleB2: There are quite a few, to be honest. The obvious one is it saves you a fair bit of money — you're not forever forking out for a mechanic. On top of that, you get to grips with how your bike works, so you can nip small problems in the bud early on. And there's real satisfaction in fixing something with your own hands.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the advantages of maintaining and repairing your own bicycle?
idioms: a stitch in time saves nine - "vaqtida qilingan bitta tikuv to'qqiztasini tejaydi"
if you want something done right, do it yourself - "to'g'ri bajarilishini xohlasang, o'zing qil"
phrases: saves money in the long run - "uzoq muddatda pul tejash"
sentenceStarters: "There are several notable advantages to…" - "…ning bir nechta muhim afzalliklari bor…"
"First and foremost, it saves money…" - "Eng avvalo, bu pul tejaydi…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several notable advantages to maintaining and repairing your own bicycle. First and foremost, it saves money in the long run — instead of paying a mechanic every time something breaks, you can fix basic issues yourself.
This also gives you a deeper understanding of how your bike works, which means you can quickly identify and solve problems before they become serious. There's also a real sense of personal satisfaction that comes from fixing something with your own hands — it's a practical skill that builds self-reliance.
Furthermore, regular maintenance extends the lifespan of your bicycle, reducing waste and being more environmentally friendly. As they say, "a stitch in time saves nine" — taking care of small repairs early prevents bigger, costlier problems later.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
O'z velosipedingizni ta'mirlash va texnik xizmat ko'rsatishning bir nechta sezilarli afzalliklari bor. Birinchi va eng muhimi, bu uzoq muddatda pulni tejaydi — har safar biror narsa buzilganda mexanikga pul to'lash o'rniga, siz o'zingiz asosiy muammolarni hal qilishingiz mumkin.

Bu, shuningdek, sizga velosipedingiz qanday ishlashini chuqurroq tushunish imkonini beradi, bu esa muammolarni jiddiy bo'lishidan oldin tezda aniqlash va hal qilish imkoniyatini beradi. O'z qo'llaringiz bilan biror narsani tuzatishdan kelib chiqadigan haqiqiy shaxsiy qoniqish hissi ham bor — bu o'ziga ishonchni mustahkamlaydigan amaliy ko'nikma.

Bundan tashqari, muntazam texnik xizmat velosipedingizning xizmat qilish muddatini uzaytiradi, chiqindilarni kamaytiradi va atrof-muhitga ko'proq foyda keltiradi. Aytishlaricha, "vaqtida qilingan bir tikuv to'qqiztasini saqlaydi" — kichik ta'mirlarga erta e'tibor berish keyinchalik katta, qimmat muammolarning oldini oladi.

questions.prompt: Why are bike-rental systems becoming popular in many cities?
questions.sampleA1: I like bikes. Many people use bikes now. Good for city.
questions.sampleA2: Bikes are good. You can rent a bike and go. It's easy and it's cheap. And you don't need to buy a bike.
questions.sampleB1: I think bike rentals are popular because it's easy to use them. You can just rent a bike for a short time. It's also good for the environment because people don't use cars. For example, in my city many people use bike rentals to go to work.
questions.sampleB2: I think it mostly comes down to convenience. You can grab a bike whenever you fancy and drop it off wherever, without the hassle of storage or repairs. On top of that, they're brilliant for the environment — they cut down on traffic and pollution, which is a huge plus in busy cities. And for tourists, it's a cheap, fun way to get around.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga velosipedlar yoqadi. Hozir ko'p odamlar velosipedlardan foydalanishadi. Shahar uchun yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Velosipedlar yaxshi. Siz velosipedni ijaraga olib, ketishingiz mumkin. Bu oson va arzon. Va sizga velosiped sotib olishingiz shart emas.
questions.uzSampleB1: Menimcha, velosiped ijarasi mashhur, chunki ulardan foydalanish oson. Siz shunchaki velosipedni qisqa vaqtga ijaraga olishingiz mumkin. Bu atrof-muhit uchun ham yaxshi, chunki odamlar mashinalardan foydalanishmaydi. Misol uchun, mening shahrimda ko'p odamlar ishga borish uchun velosiped ijarasidan foydalanishadi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Velosiped ijarasi tizimlari shaharlarda ommalashib bormoqda, menimcha, asosan ular moslashuvchan va arzon transport variantini taklif qilgani uchun. Velosipedga egalik qilishdan ko'ra ancha osonroq, ayniqsa, agar u sizga vaqti-vaqti bilan kerak bo'lsa. Bundan tashqari, bu tizimlar odamlarni mashina haydash o'rniga velosipedda yurishga undash orqali yashil shahar muhitiga hissa qo'shadi. Ular, shuningdek, ko'plab shaharlarda asosiy muammo bo'lgan tirbandlik va to'xtash muammolarini kamaytirishga yordam berishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why are bike-rental systems becoming popular in many cities?
idioms: the best of both worlds - "ikkala dunyoning eng yaxshisi"
sentenceStarters: "Bike-rental systems are becoming increasingly…" - "Velosiped ijarasi tizimlari tobora…"
"The most obvious one is…" - "Eng aniq sabab shundaki…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Bike-rental systems are becoming increasingly popular for a number of compelling reasons. The most obvious one is sheer convenience — people can pick up a bicycle at one station and drop it off at another, without worrying about storage, maintenance, or theft.
This is especially appealing in crowded cities where owning a bike can be impractical due to limited space. From an environmental perspective, bike-sharing schemes help reduce carbon emissions by offering a green alternative to cars and taxis for short trips.
They also ease traffic congestion and promote a healthier, more active lifestyle among city residents. For tourists, rental bikes are an incredibly affordable and enjoyable way to explore a new city. As the saying goes, "sharing is caring", and these systems are a perfect example of how shared resources benefit entire communities.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Velosiped ijarasi tizimlari bir qator jiddiy sabablarga ko'ra tobora ommalashib bormoqda. Eng aniq sabab - bu shunchaki qulaylik — odamlar velosipedni bir bekatdan olib, boshqa bekatga tashlab ketishlari mumkin, saqlash, texnik xizmat ko'rsatish yoki o'g'irlik haqida tashvishlanmasdan.

Bu, ayniqsa, gavjum shaharlarda dolzarb, chunki velosipedga egalik qilish joyning cheklanganligi sababli amaliy bo'lmasligi mumkin. Ekologik nuqtai nazardan, velosiped almashish sxemalari qisqa masofalarga mashina va taksiga yashil alternativa taklif qilish orqali karbonat angidrid chiqindilarini kamaytirishga yordam beradi.

Ular, shuningdek, tirbandlikni kamaytiradi va shahar aholisi o'rtasida sog'lom, faol turmush tarzini targ'ib qiladi. Sayyohlar uchun ijaraga olingan velosipedlar yangi shaharni o'rganishning nihoyatda arzon va yoqimli usuli hisoblanadi. Aytganlaridek, "ulashish - g'amxo'rlik", va bu tizimlar umumiy resurslar butun jamiyatga qanday foyda keltirishining ajoyib namunasidir.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you successfully repaired something that was broken.
questions.sampleA1: I fix toy. Toy broken. I use glue. Now okay.
questions.sampleA2: My bike had a flat tire. It was broken. I fixed it with my dad. We put air in it and now it's good. I was happy because I can ride my bike again.
questions.sampleB1: I remember once my computer mouse stopped working. I was really annoyed because I needed it for my homework. I tried changing the batteries, but that didn't work. Then, I looked online and found a suggestion to restart the computer. I did that, and surprisingly, it worked! I was so relieved I didn't have to buy a new one.
questions.sampleB2: I'd like to talk about the time I managed to fix my old desk lamp, which had suddenly stopped working right in the middle of exam season. At first I assumed it was a goner and I'd have to buy a new one, but something told me to give it a go before giving up. So I looked up a few tutorials online, unscrewed the base, and after a bit of poking around I realised one of the wires had come loose. I soldered it back into place, screwed everything together, flicked the switch — and, to my delight, it lit up straight away. Honestly, that little victory did wonders for my confidence. Up until then, I'd always assumed that fixing anything electrical was way beyond me and best left to the professionals. But once I'd pulled it off, I realised that most everyday repairs are far more manageable than they look, as long as you're patient and willing to learn. Ever since, my first instinct when something breaks is to roll up my sleeves and have a crack at it myself. As for why society should encourage repairing rather than binning things, I feel really strongly about this. We've fallen into a throwaway culture where people chuck things out at the first sign of trouble, and it's generating mountains of waste. If more of us learned to mend what we own, we'd cut down on landfill, save money, and pass on valuable skills to the next generation. At the end of the day, repairing is simply the more sustainable way to live.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men o'yinchoqni tuzatdim. O'yinchoq buzilgan edi. Men yelim ishlatdim. Hozir yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Mening velosipedimning shina teshilib qoldi. U buzilgan edi. Men uni dadam bilan tuzatdim. Biz unga havo to'ldirdik va endi u yaxshi. Men xursand bo'ldim, chunki endi yana velosipedimni minishim mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB1: Esimda, bir marta kompyuter sichqoncham ishlamay qoldi. Men juda xafa bo'ldim, chunki u menga uy vazifam uchun kerak edi. Men batareyalarni almashtirib ko'rdim, lekin bu yordam bermadi. Keyin, men internetdan kompyuterni qayta yoqish taklifini topdim. Men shunday qildim va, ajablanarlisi, bu ishladi! Men yangi sichqoncha sotib olishimga to'g'ri kelmaganidan juda xursand bo'ldim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Bir marta men kir yuvish mashinamni tuzatishga muvaffaq bo'lganman, bu men uchun katta yutuq edi. U suvni to'g'ri chiqarishni to'xtatgan edi va men katta kir yuvish uyumi bilan yuzma-yuz keldim. Darhol ustani chaqirish o'rniga, men tekshirishga qaror qildim. Bir nechta YouTube videolarini tomosha qilgandan so'ng, men suv nasosining filtri butunlay axlat bilan tiqilib qolganini aniqladim. Bu juda jirkanch edi, lekin uni tozalaganimdan so'ng, mashina yana mukammal ishladi. Men haqiqiy yutuq hissini his qildim va bu menga ko'p pulni tejashga yordam berdi.

bulletPoints: Describe a time you successfully repaired something that was broken.
How did this experience affect your confidence in solving problems?
Why is it important for society to encourage repairing items instead of throwing them away?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time I repaired something:
I'd like to talk about a time when my desk lamp suddenly stopped working. Instead of throwing it away, I decided to try and fix it myself. After watching a couple of tutorial videos online, I carefully opened it up and discovered that a loose wire had come disconnected. I managed to reconnect it, and to my delight, the lamp worked perfectly again.
How it affected my confidence:
This experience significantly boosted my confidence in problem-solving. Before that, I used to assume that fixing things required professional expertise, but I realised that many everyday repairs are actually quite straightforward if you're willing to learn. It gave me a can-do attitude — now whenever something breaks at home, my first instinct is to see if I can repair it rather than immediately replacing it.
Why society should encourage repairing:
As for why society should encourage repairing rather than discarding, I believe it's crucially important for environmental reasons. We live in a throwaway culture where people buy new items at an alarming rate, creating mountains of waste. Encouraging repairs reduces landfill waste, conserves resources, and teaches people valuable practical skills.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Biror narsani tuzatganim haqida:

Men stol chirog'im to'satdan ishlamay qolgan bir vaziyat haqida gapirmoqchiman. Uni tashlab yuborish o'rniga, o'zim tuzatishga qaror qildim. Internetda bir nechta o'quv videolarini tomosha qilganimdan so'ng, uni ehtiyotkorlik bilan ochdim va bir bo'sh sim uzilib qolganini aniqladim. Uni qayta ulashga muvaffaq bo'ldim va quvonchimga ko'ra, chiroq yana mukammal tarzda ishladi.

Bu mening ishonchimga qanday ta'sir qildi:

Bu tajriba muammolarni hal qilishdagi ishonchimni sezilarli darajada oshirdi. Ungacha men narsalarni tuzatish professional mutaxassislikni talab qiladi deb o'ylardim, lekin ko'plab kundalik ta'mirlashlar, agar o'rganishga tayyor bo'lsangiz, aslida juda oddiy ekanligini angladim. Bu menga "qo'limdan keladi" degan munosabatni berdi - endi uyda biror narsa buzilsa, birinchi fikrim uni darhol almashtirishdan ko'ra, tuzata olamanmi yoki yo'qmi, shuni ko'rish bo'ladi.

Nega jamiyat ta'mirlashni rag'batlantirishi kerak:

Jamiyat narsalarni tashlab yuborishdan ko'ra ta'mirlashni rag'batlantirishi kerakligiga kelsak, menimcha, bu atrof-muhit nuqtai nazaridan juda muhim. Biz odamlar yangi narsalarni dahshatli tezlikda sotib oladigan, chiqindilar tog'larini yaratadigan "tashlab yuborish madaniyati"da yashayapmiz. Ta'mirlashni rag'batlantirish chiqindi poligonlaridagi chiqindilarni kamaytiradi, resurslarni tejaydi va odamlarga qimmatli amaliy ko'nikmalarni o'rgatadi.

questions.prompt: Everyone should adopt a vegetarian diet to protect the planet.
questions.sampleA1: I like meat. I eat meat. Vegetables are okay.
questions.sampleA2: I like meat, and it is good. But maybe too much meat is bad. Vegetables are good for you, and maybe better for the planet.
questions.sampleB1: I think eating only vegetables is a good idea for the planet. Meat production can cause pollution. However, I like meat very much. It is difficult to stop eating meat completely, but I could eat less.
questions.sampleB2: This is a really thought-provoking topic, and I can see where both sides are coming from. On the one hand, those in favour make a compelling case. There's no denying that large-scale meat farming is one of the biggest drivers of greenhouse gas emissions — in some estimates it pumps out more than the entire transport sector. Plant-based diets also use far less land and water, so switching over could go a long way towards easing food and water shortages around the world. That said, I do think the argument has its flaws. For a start, meat is deeply woven into the traditions and cultures of countless communities, and telling people to give it up overnight would come across as heavy-handed, even disrespectful. On top of that, a sudden global shift would pull the rug out from under millions of farmers who rely on livestock to make a living. And let's not forget that some people, for medical reasons, genuinely need certain nutrients that are tricky to get from plants alone. So where do I stand? Personally, I don't think forcing everyone to go vegetarian is either realistic or fair. Instead, I'd back a middle ground — encouraging people to cut back on meat gradually and championing more sustainable farming methods. If each of us simply ate a little less meat, the collective impact would be enormous. As the saying goes, little by little, one travels far — and I reckon that gentle, steady approach would win far more hearts than any sweeping ban ever could.

Ehtimol, barqaror dehqonchilik amaliyotlarini targ'ib qilish va odamlarni ko'proq go'shtni kamroq iste'mol qilishga undash ancha erishish mumkin bo'lgan maqsad bo'lar edi.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a profoundly important debate that sits at the crossroads of health, ethics, and environmental sustainability. Supporters of a universal vegetarian diet argue that mass animal farming is one of the leading causes of global greenhouse gas emissions, contributing more than the entire transport sector in some estimates. They point out that plant-based diets require significantly less water and land to produce, which could help address food shortages.
However, opponents raise some thought-provoking counterpoints. Meat is deeply rooted in the traditions and cultures of many societies, and forcing a change would be seen as disrespectful to those cultural identities. A sudden global shift could also devastate the livelihoods of millions of farmers and workers in the meat industry. Furthermore, some individuals have specific medical or dietary requirements that make a purely vegetarian diet unsuitable for them.
In my view, rather than making it mandatory, we should encourage people to reduce their meat consumption gradually. As the saying goes, "little by little, one travels far" — small, collective changes can make a huge difference without imposing extreme measures on anyone.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu sog'liq, axloq va atrof-muhit barqarorligi chorrahasida turgan juda muhim bahs. Umumiy vegetarian parhez tarafdorlari ommaviy chorvachilik global issiqxona gazlari emissiyasining asosiy sabablaridan biri ekanligini ta'kidlaydilar va ba'zi hisob-kitoblarga ko'ra, butun transport sektoridan ham ko'proq hissa qo'shadi. Ular o'simlikka asoslangan parhezlar ishlab chiqarish uchun ancha kam suv va yer talab qilishini ta'kidlaydilar, bu esa oziq-ovqat tanqisligini bartaraf etishga yordam berishi mumkin.

Biroq, qarshilar ba'zi o'ylantiradigan qarshi fikrlarni ilgari suradilar. Go'sht ko'plab jamiyatlarning urf-odatlari va madaniyatlariga chuqur singib ketgan va o'zgarishni majburlash ushbu madaniy o'zliklarga hurmatsizlik sifatida qaraladi. Birdaniga global o'zgarish, shuningdek, go'sht sanoatidagi millionlab fermerlar va ishchilarning tirikchiligini yo'q qilishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ba'zi odamlarda sof vegetarian parhezni ular uchun yaroqsiz qiladigan maxsus tibbiy yoki parhez talablari mavjud.

Mening fikrimcha, buni majburiy qilish o'rniga, biz odamlarni go'sht iste'molini asta-sekin kamaytirishga undashimiz kerak. Maqolda aytilganidek, "tomchi tomchidan daryo bo'lur" — kichik, jamoaviy o'zgarishlar hech kimga haddan tashqari choralarni qo'llamasdan katta farq qilishi mumkin.
